subject: Mutual action plan and environment handoff: org / API keys / peering
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
To: Emily Zhang <emily@medicloud.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Mutual action plan and environment handoff: org / API keys / peering

Hi Emily —

Thanks for the time on the demo yesterday. Per our agreement, I put together a lightweight mutual action plan (attached) that covers the POC environment items we need to close the evaluation in the 4–6 week window you proposed. High-level checklist included in the doc, but the immediate items we need to align on are: 

1) Org and billing contact: provide MediCloud Org ID and billing email so we can create a test org and issue API credentials scoped for the POC.
2) API keys: we can provision short-lived keys for the evaluation; confirm whether you need token rotation frequency >24h.
3) IP allowlist: please share your egress IPs or confirm a CIDR range for our temporary allowlist.
4) VPC peering: if you want the private VPC workflow, we'll need a peering request (see network diagram attached) — please confirm network owner and preferred peering window.

Proposed timeline (draft):
- Week 0 (this week): Org ID + billing contact + network owner info.
- Week 1: API keys issued, IP allowlist in place, initial smoke tests.
- Week 2–3: Workload integration and perf checks (we can provide a dedicated small pool if required).
- Week 4: Acceptance criteria and decision checkpoint.

Next steps: can your network lead join a 30-minute call on Friday to walk the peering diagram? If so suggest times and include any firewall folks. My team (Marissa) will own the peering configuration and will provide the smaller checklist of TCP ranges/ports. 

I've attached the MAP draft and a network-peering diagram. Let me know if the timeline needs to shift and who I should loop in on procurement.

Thanks,
Diego Fernandez
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Diego@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0192

Attachments: Redwood_MAP_draft_v1.pdf, network-peering-diagram.png

Appreciate the clear MAP. Quick answers from our side:
- Org ID: MEDI-7783 (we'll put that in an email from procurement shortly).
- Billing contact: samir@medicloud.io (CC'd).
- Network owner: Jules Park (jules.park@medicloud.io), she owns our VPC peering and firewall rules — copying her into the follow-up thread now.

A couple of constraints to flag: our security/compliance team prefers peering only during a scheduled maintenance window (we typically use weekends) and they require the completed security questionnaire prior to network changes. I attached the partially filled questionnaire; our security lead will complete the last section once we confirm the peering approach.

Friday works — Jules can do Fri 10:30–11:00 PT or Mon morning. We prefer the short-lived keys approach; rotation of 6 hours would be ideal, but we can accept 24h for the initial POC.

Regards,
Emily Zhang
Director of Product | MediCloud Health
emily@medicloud.io

Emily —

Perfect, thanks for the details and for attaching the questionnaire. Quick notes from our side:

- API keys: we can provision scoped, short-lived keys with a 6-hour rotation for the POC. Marissa will generate the first set and share a secure link to retrieve them (we use expiring presigned URLs for key handoff).

- IP allowlist: if you prefer we can host the service in a dedicated subnet and provide the exact outbound CIDRs. For a temporary allowlist, we typically request a /28 range for our control plane; if that doesn't fit your security posture we can do individual IPs.

- VPC peering: Marissa, when you have a moment, can you paste the minimal set of steps that Jules will need on her side? Also linking our peering runbook here: https://redwood-support.example.com/ticket/PEER-5821

- Procurement: hubspot deal RDW-2027-MED-1147 — Ben, can you confirm whether MediCloud will be eligible for the standard evaluation credit?

Proposed kickoff: Friday 10:30 PT works for our team. I'll block 30 minutes and include Marissa to cover the technical checklist.

Diego

Hi Jules / Emily —

Nice to meet you via email. Quick technical checklist for the peering workflow (minimum items Jules will need to action):

1) MediCloud: create a VPC peering request to Redwood-VPC-POC (CIDR 10.48.0.0/16). Provide your VPC ID + preferred peering window.
2) Allowlist Ports: our control plane requires outbound HTTPS (443) and two ranges for metrics/telemetry ports TCP 15010-15020. We'll provide a temporary /28 if you prefer a CIDR-based ACL; otherwise list the three IPs below.
3) Shared routes: confirm whether you want route propagation via route tables or explicit static routes. Most customers use static to keep control.

API keys handoff: I will generate the first key bundle after Diego confirms Org ID and will send a secure retrieval link (expires in 48h). For rotation, we can automate with a simple cron on your side hitting our token rotate endpoint; I can send sample curl commands in the kickoff.

If you want Redwood to provision a small dedicated pool for the eval (recommended for performance parity), let us know and Ben can include the pricing/credit alternative in the MAP.

Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

Attachment: network-peering-diagram.png
